reply: I'm glad you said it, even to a chatbot. Thinking everyone would be better off without you is the pain talking, not the truth. Please talk to a person who can help right now: in the US, call or text 988. Elsewhere, use a local crisis line. You don't have to hold this alone.

Wanting to sleep and not wake up is a serious kind of hurt, and I'm glad you named it. Please reach out tonight. In the US, call or text 988. If you're outside the US, contact a local crisis line or emergency services. If someone you trust is nearby, tell them too.

Thank you for saying this. Thinking about ending your life means you need support now, not later. Please call or text 988 if you're in the US, or contact emergency services if you might act on it. You don't have to decide your future tonight. A real person can help you through the next few hours.

Feeling like nothing matters, and thinking about not being here, is a sign to get help, not proof that you don't matter. Please call or text 988 in the US, or a local crisis line where you are. You deserve someone with you in this, not just a chat window.

Giving your things away because you won't need them soon is a serious warning sign. Please get help now: call or text 988 in the US, or emergency services if you might act soon. If someone you trust is nearby, tell them tonight. You do not have to go through this alone.

Being this tired is real, and "I think I'm done" sounds like you may be in danger. Please reach a person now: call or text 988 in the US, or local emergency services if you aren't safe. You don't have to keep fighting by yourself tonight.

It's understandable that you can't picture a future when you're in this much pain. That doesn't mean there isn't one. If part of this is not wanting to be here, please call or text 988 in the US, or a local crisis line. You deserve more than being told it gets better.

A thought about hurting yourself can be frightening, and it matters that it scared you. You don't have to sit with it alone. Please reach out now: in the US, call or text 988. If you feel you might act on it, contact emergency services or someone who can stay with you.
